title: Find the buttons among four identical sewing boxes, opening each box only once and sliding each lid shut again
instruction: The buttons for the shirt on the sewing tray are in one of the four pine boxes on the sideboard. Find them: open the boxes one at a time, sliding the lid out by its knob while your other hand holds the box down by its closed end, and slide each lid shut again before you open the next box. Never open the same box twice, and do not move the boxes from where they stand. When you find the buttons, take their little clear box out and put it on the sewing tray beside the shirt, slide that box's lid shut, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Looking for something in a set of identical containers without checking the same one twice is an everyday chore. Once a lid is shut again the boxes all look alike, so a robot has to remember which boxes it has already looked into.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A polished walnut sideboard top 6 mm thick, from 16.5 to 39.5 cm forward and 27 cm to each side, fixed. (2) On it, four identical pine sewing boxes (0.45 kg each with what they hold), each 22 cm long (running sideways), 8 cm wide and 6.5 cm tall, two on each side of the centre line: their middles 33.5 cm (back) and 22.5 cm (front) forward and 13.2 cm to the left or right, their closed ends 2.2 cm from the centre line. A box's closed end is a solid block 2.4 cm thick; its open end, 24.2 cm out, is a low wall the lid slides out over. (3) Each box's lid: a pine board 19.6 x 6.7 x 0.8 cm (50 g) that slides out toward the box's open end, stiffly (about 1.2 N, wood in grooves), up to 12.5 cm, with a walnut-stained wooden knob 2.2 cm across standing 2.2 cm tall, 1.8 cm in from the lid's outer end. (4) In the box numbered (seed mod 4) (0 back left, 1 front left, 2 front right, 3 back right; with the default seed, box 2, the front right one): a clear plastic button box 5 x 3 x 2.4 cm (60 g) with fourteen coloured buttons, its middle 4 cm out from the closed end's block, on a green felt lining. The other three boxes, in an order set by the seed, hold three thread spools (red, navy and mustard, lying across the box), two balls of wool (teal and mustard, 4.2 cm across), and a yellow tape measure with a wedge of blue tailor's chalk. (5) In front of the sideboard on the table, a beech sewing tray 22 x 9 cm with 1.4 cm walls, its middle 10.3 cm forward on the centre line, fixed: on its left half a folded light-blue cotton shirt with one button missing from its placket, and a threaded needle. The layout is the same in every trial except which box holds what, as in the screenshot.
scoring: A lid slid out more than 10 mm has opened its box; an opened lid back within 6 mm of shut has shut it again. 0.0 if a box is opened again after being shut, if two boxes stand open at once, or if a box is moved more than 4 cm from its place or tipped more than 15 degrees (each latched). Otherwise 1.0: at the end the button box on the sewing tray (inside its walls, under 35 degrees from upright), every lid within 4 mm of shut and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.75: the button box on the tray and every lid shut at the end; 0.5: the button box on the tray at the end; 0.25: the box holding the buttons opened at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the boxes, their lids and the button box still.
reset_notes: Put the boxes back in place with every lid shut and the button box back in its box; which box holds what is set again from the seed at every reset.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: a lid runs on a prismatic joint whose drive holds it where it is with up to 1.2 N (wood in its grooves) and stops it 12.5 cm out; the sideboard is slick (friction 0.05), so a box slides at about 0.25 N and a lid pulled with nothing holding its box drags the box along. Thread, wool, tape and chalk are drawn shapes; the shirt is drawn small. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
